predictions.title: TWAP filter returns the upper adjacent order statistic
predictions.description: PanopticMath.twapFilter() computes 19 interval tick measurements, sorts them, and returns sortedTicks[10]. For 19 zero-indexed values, the median is sortedTicks[9]; sortedTicks[10] is the upper adjacent order statistic. This introduces an upward bias and allows nine manipulated high samples to influence the returned value in scenarios where ten would be required to move the true median. The resulting tick is used by PanopticPool for forced-exercise eligibility, exercise-fee calculations, liquidation valuation, and other price-sensitive decisions.
predictions.impact: An attacker who can influence enough Uniswap observation intervals may obtain an attacker-favorable oracle tick. This can affect forced-exercise authorization, exercise compensation, liquidation eligibility, collateral valuation, and liquidation bonus calculations. The exact economic impact depends on the underlying pool liquidity and position parameters.
predictions.mitigation: Return the actual median element, sortedTicks[9], or derive the index from an explicit measurement-count constant such as NUM_MEASUREMENTS / 2. Add tests covering the number of manipulated intervals required to move the returned oracle value and validate that the intended order statistic is used.

predictions.title: Solvency validation can rely solely on the short-window fast oracle
predictions.description: PanopticPool._validateSolvency() always checks solvency at fastOracleTick but checks slowOracleTick only when the absolute difference between the two exceeds MAX_SLOW_FAST_DELTA. The fast oracle is derived from only three recent observation intervals. An attacker who influences the fast oracle while keeping its difference from the slow oracle at or below 1,800 ticks can cause the account to be evaluated only at the favorable fast price. The selected tick directly affects collateral requirements, token conversion, and the final solvency decision.
predictions.impact: An undercollateralized account may pass minting, burning, premium settlement, or forced-exercise-related solvency checks at a favorable manipulated fast price. This can increase protocol exposure and may result in losses when the account later becomes insolvent.
predictions.mitigation: Require solvency at both fastOracleTick and slowOracleTick for security-sensitive operations, or calculate both outcomes and reject the operation if either fails. If only one result is used for gas reasons, select the more conservative account-specific result rather than relying solely on the numerical difference between oracle ticks. Consider strengthening the fast oracle observation horizon and adding an appropriate current-price consistency bound.

predictions.title: Forced exercise uses inconsistent and manipulable spot/TWAP prices
predictions.description: PanopticPool.forceExercise() determines exercisability using the historical twapTick but separately reads the current Uniswap spot tick from slot0().tick. It does not require the two values to be close and does not require the position to be exercisable at the current tick. The spot tick is then passed to CollateralTracker.exerciseCost(), where it controls the distance from the strike and the exponentially decaying force-exercise fee. The TWAP is also used for refund conversion. An attacker can move the spot price before forceExercise while leaving the TWAP substantially unchanged, or exploit a stale TWAP after the spot has moved, thereby affecting forced-exercise authorization and settlement.
predictions.impact: A position may be forcibly closed while it is no longer out-of-range at the current AMM price. In addition, a manipulated spot tick can reduce or otherwise distort the exercise compensation paid to the exercisee and alter token0/token1 refund composition. The resulting value transfer can disadvantage the forced-exercisee or create an unfair benefit for the exercisor.
predictions.mitigation: Add an explicit widened-int256 currentTick-versus-twapTick deviation check in forceExercise(), using a threshold appropriate for forced exercise. Additionally, require exercisability at both the oracle and current prices if current out-of-range status is required. Prefer using one validated manipulation-resistant oracle tick consistently for exercisability, strike-distance fee calculation, and refund conversion; alternatively, clamp any spot tick used for settlement to a permitted range around the oracle.

predictions.title: Spot tick influences pending premium accounting in security-sensitive paths
predictions.description: Premium calculations in PanopticPool use the current Uniswap spot tick as the atTick argument. The value is forwarded through _calculateAccumulatedPremia() and _getPremia() to SemiFungiblePositionManager.getAccountPremium(), which invokes FeesCalc.calculateAMMSwapFees(). The fee-growth calculation branches depending on whether the supplied tick is below, within, or above the liquidity range. The resulting premium affects margin balances, collateral requirements, liquidation eligibility, forced-exercise delegation, and settled-token accumulators. The settleLongPremium() path likewise reads slot0().tick and commits the resulting premium to storage.
predictions.impact: A temporary spot-price movement across a liquidity-range boundary can alter pending premium calculations. Depending on the operation, this may cause incorrect solvency outcomes, incorrect liquidation accounting, incorrect forced-exercise funding, or an incorrect amount of premium to be credited to sellers. The liquidation spot/TWAP bound limits one path but does not make the premium calculation oracle-based and does not protect the other premium-sensitive operations.
predictions.mitigation: Use a validated manipulation-resistant oracle tick for premium calculations whenever the result affects solvency, liquidation, forced exercise, or settlement. If current spot state is required for exact fee-growth accounting, apply a consistent spot/TWAP deviation bound before using the result in financial decisions and add regression tests for ticks below, inside, and above the relevant liquidity range.
